**Needs human eyes**

- **The overnight fade is the single most important thing on this board.** Six names, -4.7% to -5.5% each, in the AI/crypto complex, all *after* a green regular session.
- This is a different signal from my last four briefs: for the first time I can actually see it.
- It has the same shape as the Oct 16-21 unwind and argues for **not** chasing Wednesday AI into Thursday's open.
- **CRWV is the cleanest tell in the brief.** Wednesday: **-0.50% on RVOL 2.12** - heavy volume, no bid, while the rest of the complex rose. Overnight: **-4.84%**.
- This is the name that started the AI-credit unwind (bonds at ~15%). It is not being bought on good news and it is being sold overnight.
- **RCUS is the biggest move and it is a liquidity event, not a science event.** The casdatifan data was *good* (median OS ~35 months vs belzutifan; five brokers raised targets).
- The damage came from the concurrent **underwritten offering**.
- But at 2.92x RVOL on a $2.4B clinical-stage name with -415% operating margins, an overnight -5.86% after a -19.58% day means the exit has no bid either.
- Treat it as a broken-chart name, not a valuation opportunity.
- **SKYD's catalyst is a speech, not a deal.** Joe Malone *suggested* SpaceX could put $8-10B in. Nothing is confirmed; SpaceX, Skydance and Legendary have all declined comment in prior cases.
- SKYD is still 16% below its $9.28 NYSE opening price and the warrant overhang has not cleared.
- **Q3 on Nov 9 is the first combined Paramount-WBD quarter** - that is the real test, not the rumour.
- **NTSK's move is low-conviction and the street is under it.** RVOL 1.05 on a +10.04% day.
- Consensus PT $18.75 vs a $21.81 close - the average analyst sees it as *overvalued*. Wells Fargo at $22 is the outlier. No company news.
- **ASST's 15% preferred coupon is a structural claim ahead of the common.** ~$287M/yr of preferred dividends against a company with a steep quarterly loss, funded partly by dilutive preferred issuance, on a $335M-per-week BTC-buying pace funded by $369M of warrant exercises.
- It is a leveraged BTC proxy with a financing overhang. **Next earnings ~Nov 10.**
- **LAD is the best non-AI case study on the board:
- beat on EPS, punished on revenue mix.** Adj EPS $10.34 vs $9.70 and revenue $9.95B vs $9.75B - both beat - yet it opened ~$318 and closed $269.13, a ~15% reversal.
- Same-store revenue -1.4%, F&I -8%, net leverage 3.07x. The whole auto-retail complex (GPI, AN, ABG) sold with it. **Watch the call commentary and Q4 guide, not the headline beat.**
- **Macro calendar is dense into month-end.** **Fed Oct 27-28** (a December hike is widely expected), **10-year yield above 5.1%**, **Nov 3 midterms**,
- and **Iran talks** driving oil (WTI ~$97.50, Brent ~$109.40). Wednesday's rally was explicitly de-escalation-flavoured, on unconfirmed Iran mediation reports. A breakdown there removes the main reason the tape bid.
